By the definition in~\eqref{eq:DefEnrich} we can bound for each vertex $j\in \nodes(T)$ the right-hand side via the sum of jumps of face neighbors in the sense that

issues.failure_explanation: At boundary vertices \mathcal{E}v_h=0, so the averaging bound does not apply there; |v_h|_T(j)| is controlled only by tangential derivatives along boundary faces, which the right-hand side omits. Counterexample: take a square with four boundary edges and one interior vertex. Let v_h be continuous P1 with corner values +1,-1,+1,-1 and centre value 0. Then v_h lies in V_h and all interior jumps vanish, but \mathcal{E}v_h=0\neq v_h. Hence the right-hand side of eq:Enrichment is 0 while the left-hand side is positive.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add boundary faces to the sum, with the jump read as the trace (tangential derivative of v_h on \gamma\subset\partial\Omega). In eq:Enrichment2 and its applications, bound the boundary-face terms by the curl-bubble argument on the single adjacent element, using the zero trace of v, or trivially when v=0.
issues.overall_effect: eq:Enrichment, and hence eq:Enrichment2, are false as stated. Every result using the companion estimate is affected.
issues.title: Enrichment estimate omits boundary faces; false at boundary vertices
issues.why_classification: This is a standard local correction with routine boundary-face treatment, and all conclusions and rates survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Furthermore, we use the residual based error estimator $\eta^2_\tria = \eta^2_\tria(u_{h,n},\varepsilon)$ in \cite{DieningKreuzer08}, to estimate the distance
fewer degrees of freedom, lower energy bounds
A downside of the analysis in \cite{Kaltenbach24} is its direct use of the results in \cite{DieningKreuzer08} without a proper treatment of tangential jumps.

issues.failure_explanation: For non-conforming iterates u_{h,n}\notin V, the quantity \cJ_\varepsilon(u_{h,n})-\min_V\cJ_\varepsilon can be negative, as the paper's own 'lower energy bounds' remark indicates. It therefore cannot be equivalent to a nonnegative estimator. Moreover, the cited conforming estimator does not treat tangential jumps, which the paper itself criticises as an improper direct use.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the equivalence claim to conforming iterates. For CR, use an estimator with tangential-jump terms, or state the indicator as heuristic.
issues.overall_effect: The stated justification of the adaptive driver for the CR runs (p\le2) is unsupported. The reliability of the reported CR experiments is affected, but no theorem is.
issues.title: Conforming residual estimator claimed equivalent to energy error for CR iterates
issues.why_classification: It concerns only the description and justification of the numerical heuristics; no theoretical claim depends on it.
